assessmentSummary.identity: A stationary side-specific split squat with the rear foot placed on a stable declared support, whole lead foot on the floor, controlled descent through declared pain-free range, lead-leg-biased ascent, and return to the same balanced rear-foot-elevated stance.
currentCardFindings: Bulgarian Split Squat and rear-foot-elevated legacy sources preserve the same support geometry and dynamic repetition action.
Dumbbell, barbell, kettlebell, stable-hand-support, and slow-eccentric executions are exact variants when rear support, stance, load position, and tempo are declared.
Floor split squats, front-foot elevation, isometric holds, suspension support, jumping to a box, and stepping lunges change support, contraction, or ordered action and remain distinct or review-only.
The title phrase Beginner to Advanced on one media candidate is only a video title and is not exercise-card proficiency metadata.
Five direct video candidates have title, channel, and oEmbed metadata only; no playback or human exact-variant, safety, caption, accessibility, or approval review has occurred.

proposedDosage.capacity: 2-5 sets of 3-10 quality repetitions per side with 90-240 seconds recovery according to load and objective
proposedDosage.resilience: 2-4 sets of 5-8 controlled repetitions per side at submaximal load with 75-180 seconds recovery
proposedDosage.progressWhen: both sides preserve support, entry and exit, lead-foot pressure, knee path, pelvis, trunk, range, tempo, breathing, finish, and load control

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Retain one stable Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat identity, with Bulgarian Split Squat as an alias and exact support, implement, load-position, and tempo variants. Keep all candidates, graph edges, calibrations, and publication state quarantined for human review.

currentCardSnapshot.description: From a stationary side-specific split stance, place the rear foot on a stable declared support and keep the whole lead foot on the floor. Declare support height/contact, lead side, stance, support, implement, load position, load, range, tempo, repetitions, rest, and finish. Brace, lower through the owned pain-free range, then drive through the lead leg to the same balanced rear-foot-elevated stance.

population.medicalScope: This card is not diagnosis, rehabilitation, or medical clearance; follow the athlete care plan and local scope.

evidence.sourceTitle: Muscle Activation in Unilateral Barbell Exercises: Implications for Strength Training and Rehabilitation
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: The cited study treats floor-based split squat and rear-foot-elevated split squat as separately named unilateral barbell exercises.
Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat uses the exact support geometry declared by its card; implement, load position, hand support, and tempo are variants, not athlete proficiency levels.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of step lengths on biomechanical characteristics of lower extremity during split squat movement
claims: Split-squat stance length changes lower-extremity kinematics, kinetics, and measured muscle activity.
Declare lead side, stance, support contact, trunk strategy, range, implement, load position, tempo, and finish; stepping lunges, isometric holds, and jumps remain separate actions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Muscle Activation in Unilateral Barbell Exercises: Implications for Strength Training and Rehabilitation
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: The study measured vastus lateralis, biceps femoris, gluteus maximus, and gluteus medius activity during split-squat variants.
The card declares lead foot, ankle, knee, hip, pelvis, trunk, optional upper-extremity load handling, sagittal motion, multiplanar stabilization, and side-specific asymmetrical support.

evidence.sourceTitle: Rear Leg-derived Moment Contributes to Resistance Against Hip Extension in Bulgarian Split Squats
claims: Rear-foot-elevated split-squat mechanics change with stance width and trunk angle, and the rear leg can contribute resistance against lead-hip extension.

Observable gates include exact support contact, stationary feet, whole lead-foot pressure, controlled knee path, organized pelvis and trunk, owned range, lead-leg-biased ascent, balance, and safe entry and exit.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of step lengths on biomechanical characteristics of lower extremity during split squat movement
claims: Support geometry, stance, range, load, and fatigue alter the coordination and physical demands of an exact split-squat execution.
Score only exercise complexity and physical difficulty for each exact variant and derive overall difficulty as their maximum; do not assign an exercise-card skill or proficiency level.

evidence.sourceTitle: Muscle Activation in Unilateral Barbell Exercises: Implications for Strength Training and Rehabilitation
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: Relative loading and proximity to fatigue affect interpretation of lower-extremity muscle activity in unilateral exercises.
Track lead-leg fatigue, stabilization demand, optional grip and bracing fatigue, eccentric exposure, side differences, technical change, and recovery without claiming one universal load.

evidence.sourceTitle: Rear Leg-derived Moment Contributes to Resistance Against Hip Extension in Bulgarian Split Squats
claims: Rear support, stance width, and trunk orientation are meaningful execution conditions rather than interchangeable setup details.

Require a level high-traction surface, stable support when elevated, clear station, exact implement and load, controlled pickup and set-down, pain-free range, safe side change, and adequate coach sightline.

evidence.sourceTitle: Resistance training prescription for muscle strength and hypertrophy in healthy adults: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
claims: Resistance-training outcomes vary with load, sets, frequency, and outcome specificity; no single prescription is optimal for every purpose.
Use side-balanced quality sets, record actual repetitions and load, and stop before stance, support, knee, pelvis, trunk, breathing, tempo, or load-control quality changes.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of step lengths on biomechanical characteristics of lower extremity during split squat movement
claims: Because stance length changes mechanics, setup instructions must preserve an individualized repeatable stance.
State the lead side and support, keep the front foot connected, lower through owned range, track the knee, drive through the lead leg, finish in the same stance, and exit or set down safely.

evidence.sourceTitle: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
evidence.sourcePublisher: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
claims: Resistance-training prescription should be individualized to the outcome, exercise, dose, and person rather than driven by a universal fatigue target.
Stop for pain, pinching, numbness, giving way, dizziness, support movement, balance loss, uncontrolled joint or trunk motion, unsafe load handling, missed tempo, grinding, or a changed repetition.

evidence.sourceTitle: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
evidence.sourcePublisher: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
claims: Load, volume, effort, and specificity materially affect resistance-training adaptations.

Choose the exact support and load variant from current ability, symptoms, objective, logistics, cumulative unilateral-leg and trunk fatigue, duration, and safe failure options; athlete readiness is not stored as an exercise skill level.

evidence.sourceTitle: Validity and Reliability of the Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat 5 Repetition Maximum to Determine Unilateral Leg Strength Symmetry
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: Side-specific RFESS performance can be measured repeatably under a declared test protocol, but interpretation depends on the exact loading and protocol.
Expose side, stance, support, implement, load, range, tempo, repetitions, rest, expected sensations, self-checks, stop signal, and after-set reporting in plain language.

evidence.sourceTitle: Rear Leg-derived Moment Contributes to Resistance Against Hip Extension in Bulgarian Split Squats
claims: Stance, trunk position, and rear-limb contribution affect rear-foot-elevated split-squat mechanics.

Coach support should expose station and support inspection, side and stance, lead-foot and knee path, rear-leg contribution, pelvis and trunk, range, load, tempo, fatigue, symptoms, substitutions, and shutdown actions.

evidence.sourceTitle: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
evidence.sourcePublisher: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
claims: Resistance exercise can be individualized across equipment, load, volume, and effort while retaining outcome specificity.

Accessibility options include stable hand support, floor-based support, bodyweight loading, adjusted stance, shorter pain-free range, fewer repetitions, longer rest, and written, audio, still-image, walkthrough, or live instruction.

evidence.sourceTitle: Muscle Activation in Unilateral Barbell Exercises: Implications for Strength Training and Rehabilitation
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: Floor split squat, single-leg squat, and rear-foot-elevated split squat are treated as distinct exercise conditions.

Implement and tempo changes can remain variants, while rear- or front-foot elevation, stepping, isometric contraction, perturbation, takeoff, flight, and landing change identity or require explicit review.
YouTube supports privacy-enhanced embedding through youtube-nocookie.com.

alternateAssessments.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: Bulgarian Split Squat is retained as the common alias for rear-foot-elevated split squat.

alternateAssessments.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: Dumbbells change grip, load position, pickup, and set-down within the same rear-foot-elevated action.

alternateAssessments.name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: Back-rack loading changes bracing, supervision, failure consequence, and rack requirements.

alternateAssessments.name: Kettlebell Bulgarian Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: A declared kettlebell hold and load preserve the rear-foot-elevated action.

alternateAssessments.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat Negative
alternateAssessments.rationale: Slow lowering preserves the action while changing tempo, eccentric stress, duration, and fatigue.

alternateAssessments.name: Floor-Based Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: Rear-forefoot floor contact changes support geometry and is retained as the Split Squat card.

alternateAssessments.name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: Elevating the lead foot instead of the rear foot changes support geometry and range.

alternateAssessments.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat Isometric Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: A fixed hold changes contraction type and dose from dynamic repetitions.

alternateAssessments.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat Jump to Box
alternateAssessments.rationale: Takeoff, flight, target box, impact, and terminal landing add ordered actions.

alternateAssessments.name: Suspension Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: Suspended rear-foot support may preserve the action but changes stability and requires exact review.

alternateAssessments.name: Forward-Lean Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: Trunk angle changes joint demand and must be declared without creating an athlete level.

alternateAssessments.name: Supported Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
alternateAssessments.rationale: Stable hand support preserves the action while reducing balance and failure demand.
